 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The MLB offseason is already delivering some major moves, and the Chicago White Sox have reportedly landed a World Series champion.
 Chicago has agreed to a three-year contract worth $52.5 million with right-handed starting pitcher Dustin May, taking him away from the Milwaukee Brewers after their championship-winning 2026 campaign.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement According to MLB insider Robert Murray , the White Sox and May agreed to the deal Tuesday morning. Fellow MLB insider Jon Heyman confirmed the agreement and reported that the contract is worth $52.5 million over three seasons.
 The move gives Chicago an experienced starting pitcher as the organization looks to build on its recent postseason appearance.
 MORE: Pete Crow-Armstrong is only player in MLB history to accomplish these 5 feats in a single season 
 Dustin May leaves Milwaukee after World Series win
 Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Dustin May (21) pitches during the first inning against the Tampa Bay Rays during Game 4 of the World Series at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Fla. on Oct 27, 2026.
 May began the 2026 season with the St. Louis Cardinals before being traded to the Brewers in early August. Across 31 combined regular-season starts with the two organizations, the right-hander posted a 7-9 record with a 4.31 ERA.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement He recorded 145.2 innings pitched during the regular season before Milwaukee's postseason run.
 May appeared in five postseason games for the Brewers, including two starts, as the team captured the World Series championship. He surrendered 11 hits and seven earned runs across 11 innings during the 2026 playoffs.
 Although his postseason numbers weren't spectacular, May was part of a Milwaukee team that ultimately reached the sport's biggest prize.
 Now, he'll have an opportunity to establish himself with a new organization after spending the final months of the season in Milwaukee.

 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement White Sox add another piece for 2027
 Oct 24, 2026; Milwaukee, Wisconsin, USA; Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Dustin May (21) pitches during the fifth inning against the Tampa Bay Rays in game two of the 2026 World Series at American Family Field. Mandatory Credit: Michael McLoone-Imagn Images
 May brings plenty of MLB experience to Chicago despite still having room to develop as a starting pitcher.
 Through 102 career appearances, including 88 starts, he has compiled a 26-29 record with a 4.12 ERA and a 1.237 WHIP across 469.2 innings.
 The White Sox are coming off a postseason appearance that ended with a five-game elimination against the Cleveland Guardians in the American League Division Series.
 Adding a World Series champion to the starting rotation could be an important step as Chicago looks to remain competitive and make another postseason push.
 For Milwaukee, losing May represents another departure following a championship season. Meanwhile, the White Sox are betting that the right-hander can provide valuable innings and help strengthen their rotation over the next three years.
